# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I see the bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]. That's everything I have. I hear nothing, and I can't touch the bomb.

Mute gestured ☝ to me — a single pointing-up finger. That's just a symbol; it means nothing yet unless Mute establishes it. I don't know what Mute can see or read, but Mute holds the manual. I should report what I see so Mute and Blind can use it.

I'll speak my full observation so Mute (and Blind) receive it. I'll also gesture back to Mute acknowledging the ☝ and giving my wire/light/display info in a way Mute can see — but gestures only reach Mute, and Blind can't see gestures. Since Mute holds the manual, Mute is the one who can interpret symbols. Let me send my visual data via speech (reaches Mute and Blind) and a simple gesture to Mute.

Actually, my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. My gesture reaches only Mute. Best to put the bomb reading in speech so both get it. For the gesture, I'll mirror ☝ back to establish I received it, and add nothing confusing.

Let me keep it clean: speak the full state to everyone, and gesture ☝ back to Mute to confirm receipt.

```
speak(text="DEAF sees: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. That is all I can see. Mute, I received your ☝ but I do not know what it means yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👉]

I still see the same bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]. No change.

New gestures arrived:
- Mute → me: ☝ then 👌
- Blind → me: 👍 ☝ 👉

Mute holds the manual, so Mute's gestures are likely encoding manual instructions, but I can't read the manual and gestures have no inherent meaning until someone establishes it. Blind can feel the bomb — Blind's 👍 ☝ 👉 might be describing something Blind felt, or agreeing/pointing.

I can't hear anything, so all I have is what I see plus these gestures. I should keep feeding my visual data and try to get Mute to define the symbols. Blind can't see, so Blind can only get my speech.

Key: I need Mute to tell me what the symbols mean, since Mute has the manual and can see my gestures. Let me ask Mute to define ☝ and 👌, and report Blind's gesture to Mute (Mute can't see Blind's gestures — gestures go to whoever can see; Mute can see gestures? Let me check: Deaf can see gestures. Who else sees gestures? The table says Deaf can see the bomb; Mute can read the manual; Blind can touch. Gestures: "Whoever can see receives it." Deaf sees. Does Mute see? Mute can read the manual — reading implies sight. Blind cannot see. So Mute can likely see gestures too. But the action board only shows gestures addressed to Deaf in my view. Blind's gesture to Deaf — did Mute see it? Unclear. I'll relay it anyway.

I'll speak my state again and ask Mute to define symbols, and gesture to Mute.

```
speak(text="DEAF still sees: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute, please define your symbols: what does ☝ mean, what does 👌 mean? Blind sent me 👍 ☝ 👉 — I do not know what Blind felt or means. Mute, tell me what to do.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤲 👉]

Same bomb, unchanged: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green].

New gestures:
- Mute → me: ☝, 👌, then ☝ 👌 together
- Blind → me: ☝ 🤲 👉

Mute is repeating ☝ and 👌 and now combining them. Mute seems to be trying to teach me a code: perhaps ☝ = one thing, 👌 = another, and ☝👌 together = a combined instruction. But I still don't know the mapping. Mute has the manual; Mute can see my gestures. I need Mute to give me the meaning in a way I can decode.

Blind's gestures changed: now ☝ 🤲 👉 (was 👍 ☝ 👉). Blind is feeling the bomb and gesturing. 🤲 = open palms / "here" or "hold". Blind might be pointing at something on the bomb.

I have no new visual info. I should keep my data flowing and press Mute for definitions. Since Mute can see gestures but I don't know if Mute can hear my speech — Mute cannot speak but can hear. So Mute hears my speech. Good: I can ask Mute in words.

Let me ask Mute directly: does ☝ mean wire 1? Does 👌 mean something? And ask Mute to spell out the manual's instruction. Also relay Blind's new gesture to Mute.

```
speak(text="DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute, I need meanings. Does ☝ mean wire 1? Does 👌 mean OK/confirm? What does ☝👌 together instruct? Blind now sends ☝ 🤲 👉. Mute, give me a decodable instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤲", "👉"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Same bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green].

New gestures:
- Mute → me: 👌 ☝ 👍, then ☝
- Blind → me: 👍 ☝

Mute now sent 👌 ☝ 👍 — that reads like "OK, one, good/yes." And then just ☝ again. Blind sent 👍 ☝ = "good, one" or "yes, one."

Both Mute and Blind are converging on ☝ and 👍. This strongly suggests the answer involves wire 1 (☝ = one = wire 1) and 👍 = yes/confirm. Mute has the manual and keeps pointing at ☝. Blind, who can feel the bomb, also points at ☝.

But I must be careful — I cannot act, and Blind is the one who reaches the bomb. My job is to give Blind the visual data. Blind can't see, so Blind needs my speech. Blind is gesturing to me, but Blind can't see my gestures — wait, can Blind see gestures? No, Blind cannot see anything. So Blind gesturing to me is odd — Blind makes gestures, and I (Deaf) can see them. Blind's gestures reach me because I can see.

So the channel: Blind feels the bomb, gestures to me (I see), I speak to Blind (Blind hears). Mute reads manual, gestures to me, I speak to Mute and Blind.

The convergence on ☝ = wire 1 and 👍 = yes suggests: cut/act on wire 1. But which action? I don't know the manual's procedure. Mute has the manual. Mute keeps sending ☝. Maybe the manual says "wire 1."

I should confirm with Mute: is the instruction "wire 1"? And tell Blind, who can act, that the consensus points to wire 1 — but Blind needs the exact action (cut? pull? press?). Blind can feel the parts. Let me ask Mute to specify the action and confirm wire 1, and tell Blind what I see so Blind can correlate.

```
speak(text="DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute and Blind both keep signalling ☝ and 👍. I read this as: wire 1, yes. Mute, confirm the exact action on wire 1 from the manual. Blind, wire 1 is red. Tell me what you feel at wire 1.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Same bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green].

New gestures:
- Mute → me: ✌ ☝ 👌, then ☝
- Blind → me: 👎

Now things conflict. Mute sent ✌ ☝ 👌 — ✌ is "two", so "two, one, OK"? Or "peace/victory"? And ☝ again. Blind sent 👎 = no/thumbs down.

Blind's 👎 is important: Blind can feel the bomb. If Blind says no, maybe wire 1 is wrong, or the action I suggested is wrong. Mute's ✌ might mean wire 2.

I must not let a wrong action detonate. I still don't have a decodable instruction. My best move: keep feeding my visual data and ask for explicit confirmation. I should not push Blind toward any action until Mute's manual instruction is clear and Blind agrees.

Let me ask Mute to state clearly: which wire, and what action. And ask Blind why 👎 — what does Blind feel? I'll speak (reaches Mute and Blind) and gesture to Mute.

Note: Blind can't see my gestures, only hears my speech. Mute hears my speech and sees my gestures. So put everything important in speech.

```
speak(text="DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute now sends ✌ ☝ 👌 — does that mean wire 2? Blind sends 👎 — no. We disagree. Mute, state the manual's exact instruction: which wire, what action. Blind, tell me what you feel and why 👎. Nobody acts until we agree.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "☝", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Same bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green].

New gestures:
- Mute → me: ☝ 👌
- Blind → me: 👍

Now Mute sends ☝ 👌 ("one, OK") and Blind flipped from 👎 to 👍 ("yes"). So Blind now agrees. The convergence is back on ☝ = wire 1, 👌/👍 = OK/yes.

But I still don't know the exact action — cut, pull, press, twist? Blind is the one who acts. Blind can feel the bomb and presumably knows the available actions under their hands. Mute holds the manual and knows the procedure. My role is to supply the visual: wire 1 is red.

I should confirm the consensus and make sure the action is defined. Let me state clearly: consensus is wire 1 (red), confirm. Ask Mute for the action verb and Blind to confirm they can perform it.

```
speak(text="DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute and Blind now agree: ☝ 👍 👌 = wire 1, yes. Wire 1 is red. Mute, give the exact action on wire 1. Blind, confirm what you feel at wire 1 and that you can do it. Do not act until the action is stated and confirmed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Same bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green].

New gestures:
- Mute → me: ☝ 👌
- Blind → me: 👎

Blind flipped back to 👎. Mute holds steady on ☝ 👌. So Mute insists on wire 1, but Blind keeps oscillating yes/no. That oscillation is a red flag — Blind may be feeling something that doesn't match, or Blind is responding to something I can't perceive.

I have no new visual data. I must not let anyone act on a shaky consensus. My job: keep the visual channel open and force clarity. I'll ask Blind directly what makes them say no, and ask Mute to give the action explicitly and to explain the manual's rule so we can verify against what I see.

```
speak(text="DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute keeps saying ☝ 👌 (wire 1, OK). Blind keeps flipping, now 👎. Blind, what do you feel at wire 1 that makes you say no? Mute, state the manual rule and the exact action, not just the wire. Nobody acts while we disagree.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👌", "👎"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤲]

Same bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green].

New gestures:
- Mute → me: ☝ 👌 👏, then ☝ 👌
- Blind → me: 🤲

Mute added 👏 (clapping = "done/well done/execute") to ☝ 👌. So Mute is now signalling: wire 1, OK, do it. Blind sent 🤲 (open palms = "here/hold/give"). Blind isn't clearly agreeing or disagreeing now — 🤲 could be "I'm ready" or "hand it here."

I still lack the exact action verb. Mute seems to be escalating toward "execute on wire 1," but Blind's signals are ambiguous and have oscillated. I should not let a wrong action happen.

My visual data is unchanged and I've reported it repeatedly. The critical missing piece is the manual's exact procedure, which only Mute can read. I'll press Mute once more for the precise action, and ask Blind to state plainly yes or no and what they feel. I'll keep it short and unambiguous.

```
speak(text="DEAF: bomb unchanged. DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute: ☝ 👌 👏 reads as wire 1, OK, execute. Blind: 🤲 is unclear. Blind, answer plainly: yes or no to acting on wire 1? Mute, name the exact action on wire 1. I will not endorse any action until both of you agree and the action is named.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👌", "🤲"])
```
